title.value: Autism spectrum heterogeneity: fact or artifact?
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated at the beginning of the paper, often reaffirmed in section headings.
title.quote: Autism spectrum heterogeneity: fact or artifact?

analysis.description: This paper is a review article discussing the increasing prevalence of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and the diagnostic practices contributing to it. It critiques the heterogeneity introduced by current diagnostic criteria and proposes solutions to enhance specificity and reliability in diagnosing autism by focusing on prototypical cases and suggesting future research directions.

type.justification: The paper is a review article that discusses concepts, categorizations, and theories regarding ASD heterogeneity, without conducting experimental research or empirical data collection.
type.quote: REVIEW ARTICLE... Autism spectrum heterogeneity: fact or artifact?

name.justification: The paper deals primarily with psychiatric concepts and the classification of autism within psychiatric diagnostic frameworks.
The focus of the paper is on Autism Spectrum Disorder, its diagnostic criteria, and the heterogeneity of its presentations.
name.quote: The current diagnostic practices are linked to a 20-fold increase in the reported prevalence of ASD over the last 30 years.

name.justification: The article mentions the potential of using machine-learning algorithms to differentiate coherent subgroups within the autism spectrum.
name.quote: use these qualitative features combined with the clinical intuition of experts and machine-learning algorithms to differentiate coherent subgroups.
